description: Version 3 terms under the gpu-reservation/1 template, for a booking that relies on other bookings. They are version 2 terms with the header's version set to 3 and one more section, dependencies, a list of one to four entries, each naming a different booking relied on (a commitment reference with kind, chainId, lock, commitmentId, side and termsHash, on the buyer side), the condition it has to meet ("accepted") and the section of it the seller shows ("subject"). The five version 2 sections are hashed exactly as version 2 hashes them, with salt info "avow:terms:v2:salt:<section>" and label "avow:terms:v2:<section>". The dependencies section has salt info "avow:terms:v3:salt:dependencies" and label "avow:terms:v3:dependencies", and each entry's lock, commitmentId and termsHash are written in lower case before it is hashed. The terms hash is keccak256(abi.encode(string "avow:terms:v3", string headerJson, bytes32 subject, bytes32 consideration, bytes32 remedies, bytes32 resolution, bytes32 backing, bytes32 dependencies)). lockTerms is what Avow's approval carries for a 6-decimal token, the same mapping as version 2, since the lock enforces nothing in the dependencies section. subjectShownAlone shows the subject with its own salt and the other five section hashes. The header holds dependencyCheck, "buyer" when the buyer reads each booking relied on from the chain itself and "avow" when Avow checks them for it. In the last vector Avow checks the booking relied on, and its elided field is the buyer's view of the terms, every section in clear with its own salt under salts except dependencies, which is its label "avow:terms:v3:dependencies" and its digest, the section hash. The buyer's view gives the same terms hash, from the header, each shown section hashed with its salt, and the digest. invalid lists version 3 terms that differ from the first vector only in their dependencies section or their dependencyCheck, each with the reason a version 3 reader refuses them, and invalidElided lists views of the last vector a buyer refuses, each with its reason.
